sentence: This project makes gamma-herpesviruses with defined mutations to help find traits of cancer-causing herpesviruses that depend on a kind of RNA.
This project builds a microelectrode array that senses neurotrophic factors and tests sensory neuron function in a tooth root organoid made from post-natal cells.
This project studies how gut dysbiosis in aged mice affects recovery after traumatic brain injury, using microbiome changes and germ-free mice.
This project maintains and builds a web tool that lets researchers view and interpret large cancer genomic data sets from tumor samples.
This project tries to find out how a subset of liver cells affects inflammation and immune regulation in alcohol-associated hepatitis.
This project tries to find out which sickle cell disease medications work best for which groups of patients and which genes predict response.
This project studies how mutations shape the immune environment of diffuse large B cell lymphoma and builds a score to predict immunotherapy response.
This project holds a workshop where imaging scientists share magnetic resonance methods that go beyond traditional proton imaging.
This project studies how stress disrupts dopamine signaling and reward processing.
This project tries to find out how astrocytes, a brain cell type, affect waking up from anesthesia with volatile anesthetics.
This project tries to find out which gene expression regulators are needed for sensory cells to develop in the hearing organ.
This project studies where differences between tumor cells in gastric cancer come from and how to target them to improve therapy.
This project supports research in cell and molecular biology, microbiology, genetics, immunology and neurobiology.
This project studies how high levels of DNA replication stress in small cell lung cancer make tumors vulnerable to treatment.
This project provides data science support for precision medicine studies, including artificial intelligence, deep-learning and analysis of proteomic and metabolomic data.
This project supports cancer clinical trials that test treatments for patients with prostate cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer, melanoma, myeloma and leukemia.
This project studies the gene regulatory network that guides early cell fate decisions in mammalian embryos.
This project looks for genetic variants that cause inflammatory bowel disease and tests their effects in human T cells.
This project studies what controls cardiac fibrosis, a condition linked to heart failure.
This project provides imaging tools, such as magnetic resonance imaging and fiber photometry, to study how alcohol changes brain circuits.
